content_voiceover: This page asks which combination of statements about genomic targets and their commercially available agents in AML is correct. Statement one, that FLT3 internal tandem duplication mutations raise relapse risk and worsen outcomes while FLT3 TKD mutations are prognostically neutral, is true. Statement two, that sorafenib and midostaurin have shown efficacy in both de novo and relapsed refractory AML, is also true. Statement three, that venetoclax as a single agent and in combination with chemotherapy has shown early promising results in adult AML, is true as well. Statement four, however, claims that adding up front gemtuzumab ozogamicin provides no benefit in pediatric AML, and this is false, since pediatric trials such as AAML0531 demonstrated that adding gemtuzumab ozogamicin to induction chemotherapy actually improved outcomes in children with AML. So the correct combination is statements one, two, and three together, giving answer B.
keypoints: FLT3-ITD worsens outcomes and raises relapse risk; FLT3-TKD is prognostically neutral
Sorafenib and midostaurin show efficacy in both de novo and relapsed refractory AML
Venetoclax shows promising results as monotherapy and in combination in adult AML
Gemtuzumab ozogamicin actually improves outcomes when added to pediatric AML induction
keypoint_voiceover: Statements one, two, and three are all correct, FLT3 ITD is adverse while TKD is neutral, sorafenib and midostaurin work in both de novo and relapsed disease, and venetoclax shows early promise in adults. The trap is statement four, gemtuzumab ozogamicin actually does help in pediatric AML.
